Ecosystem Health Scoreboard Nov 2026 · run 01‑11

This is a sanitised public scoreboard; the full private record, with every path and finding, lives on Drive.

Migration Integrity Index 62/100 (tracked separately). Composite is flat, but the mix improved: Architecture rose on two closed reds — Google-native stubs are down to 0 (was 12) and the credential scan holds at PASS(0) — while Redundancy slipped a point as unfiled intake piled up.

Score trend · v3 scoring basis (full tree, Drive API)

Recent v3-basis runs, 62 → 66 → 66 — the jump to 66 last month held this month. The gap to the 85 "runs unattended and trusted" ceiling is the standing work below, now led by knowledge-base synthesis rather than security.

1 · What this run did

Measured

  • Full-tree census through the Drive API, cloud-only — the laptop was never in the loop. Batched breadth-first over the whole workspace; archive and backups excluded from the score.
  • Kernel-vs-memory drift check: CLEAR. The rules on disk and in the cross-surface memory floor agree in substance; the check ran against the live files, not the lagging project-doc snapshot.
  • Credential scan across the tree — the first-class security pass: 0 secrets at rest.
  • Four-pillar score recomputed from this run's census; every figure traces to an API pull.

Published (create-only, nothing moved or deleted)

  • Private master record written to Drive with the full, unsanitised detail — paths, findings, the reversible archive list.
  • Dated history + scheduler snapshot appended as new files (the audit trail is never overwritten).
  • This scoreboard mirrored verbatim to the public handoff file for the publisher step to push.
  • No autonomous delete, move, or rename — every cleanup is proposed as a list for a human to action by hand.

6 · Action plan · owner: operator

  1. Restart the parked synthesis work.THIS MONTH It is the single lever on the knowledge-base synthesis floor — the system hoards raw intake and rarely distils it. With security and stubs closed, this is now the #1 durable drag.
  2. Fix the monthly routine that still points at merged knowledge bases.BEFORE NEXT FIRE One enabled routine lists knowledge bases that were consolidated away in September; left as-is it hunts for sources that no longer exist. A prompt-list edit.
  3. Sort the unfiled intake and trim the operating-memory register.THIS MONTH Intake has accumulated unsorted, and the working-memory file is over its self-imposed size budget — both drag the structure score and both are routine housekeeping.
  4. Re-sync the project-doc kernel copies and clear the by-hand hygiene list.WHEN CONVENIENT The mounted-session kernel mirror lags the canonical on-disk copy; a couple of duplicate-suffix files and incidental empty folders remain. All reversible, all in the private record; the audit will not touch files unattended.
  5. Wire the health artifact update.SETUP This cloud run has no artifact tool, so the database write is owed. The public site is fed by this handoff regardless.

The one human decision that is the bottleneck

For the first time, the bottleneck is not security. The two reds that dominated this board for months — plaintext credentials and Google-native stubs — are both closed and verified this run. What is left is a content decision only a human makes: restart the knowledge-base synthesis work so the system starts distilling the raw material it has been hoarding. Everything else on this board is hygiene the system proposes but cannot execute. The machine censused, scored, confirmed the two remediations, published cloud-only, and pushed the scoreboard — nothing destroyed.

Sanitised scoreboard. It carries only the score, per-pillar RAG and deltas, trend, plain counts, guardrail PASS/FAIL, and the credential-scan count + PASS/FAIL. It never carries a secret value or path, a file or folder listing, a person's name, an inbox detail, a private financial figure, or an automation trigger URL — those stay in the private .md record on Drive.
